title: Causal memory × condition-blind learned addressing × measured sparse computation
question: Can opposite-past paired histories yield accurate retrieval and execution despite intervening confusable writes, with counted selective work lower than exhaustive scanning?
held_constant: five preregistered seeds; 3 history levels, 4 write-count levels, 3 K budgets, 4 interference strengths
same-present opposite-past matched histories with identical current observations and independent distractors
original 2026-10-09 thresholds and evaluation grid unchanged
selective path cannot silently scan history; total measured work includes index maintenance
no generic learned CASM executor is claimed validated

endpoints.name: joint_integrated_capability_and_work
endpoints.description: All original threshold checks in thresholds object are jointly required; no single mean can mask a condition failure

decision_rule.condition: All integrity checks pass and every registered threshold in thresholds passes
decision_rule.licenses: Bounded positive synthetic joint memory, retrieval and work evidence
decision_rule.does_not_license: General computation, arbitrary capabilities, AGI or sublinear total work if the index scans history

decision_rule.condition: Integrity checks pass but one or more registered thresholds fail
decision_rule.licenses: Measured negative or partial integration outcome with full cell breakdown

decision_rule.condition: Any data leakage, missing episode, instrumentation defect, or provenance failure

interpretation_order: verify immutable preregistration, training/eval namespace separation and source hashes
verify matched past/current and distinct confusable target writes
verify all model-visible inputs and no label/slot/channel leaks
verify train parameter/gradient and state-write integrity
verify exact memory, address, and execution arm coverage
verify per-seed per-condition capability and paired causal controls
apply all frozen decision thresholds and claim boundaries
